summary: Say the counting numbers in order up to 30, and start counting from a number other than one.
Count 10 or more objects, touching each one once while saying one number for it.
Know that the last number said when counting a group tells how many there are in all.
Look at a small group of 1 to 5 things and say how many without counting.
Look at any written number up to 10 and say its name, knowing all of them.
Count two groups and say which has more, fewer, or if they are the same.
Show that adding one thing to a small group, or taking one away, changes it by exactly one.
Split a small group into two parts in different ways, and join two small groups into one.
Solve everyday adding and taking-away problems with objects, up to a total of 10.
Share a group of objects out fairly so two or more people each get the same number.
Sort objects into groups by one feature, or by two, like color and then size.
Copy and continue repeating patterns like AABB or ABC, and say which part repeats.
Make up different repeating patterns, or build a pattern again with other objects.
Put two things side by side to compare their length, weight or how much they hold, and talk about it.
Line up four or five objects in order by length, height or how much they hold.
Measure how long something is by laying objects like paper clips end to end.
Show data with objects, tally marks or a picture graph, with one mark for each item.
With help, count and compare the groups in a chart or graph to see which has more or less.
Name, describe and make circles, squares, triangles and rectangles, talking about sides and corners.
Recognize a few solid shapes, such as a sphere, a cube and a cylinder.
Tell if two flat shapes are the same shape whatever their size or turn, and compare sides and corners.
Put flat or solid shapes together to make a picture or a model, like a house from blocks.
Say where things are using words like on, under, near, far, between, in front of and behind.
Turn, flip or slide a piece in your head to see where it fits, with less trial and error.
